support_policy: Every entry is a candidate. Support requires exact artifact, converter, backend, and physical-target evidence.

models.note: Approximately 5.1B total including embedding tables; E2B denotes effective computation, not total weight count. Verify instruction-tuned variant at import.
Model card lists 25.2B parameters and 3.8B active, with a separate vision encoder. Verify the selected instruction-tuned text path.

35B language parameters, about 3B active. The project has not converted these upstream weights itself. The separately enrolled prequantized GGUF has physical-phone streaming and bounded JSON/SSE API evidence; neither establishes full-resident reference parity or general converter compatibility.
Newer dense model, not the initial expert-streaming target.

Text-only derived GGUF; the exact artifact runs on the physical phone at context 512. Greedy token IDs diverge from the x86 host after the first token, so no cross-architecture numerical parity is claimed.

Integration fixture, not a catalog target. The exact artifact completed storage-backed expert streaming on the phone with identical tokens across seven runs. No full-resident reference parity was obtained; the synthetic runtime gate is bitwise. Peak process RSS was about 1.2 GiB after mmap prefetch was disabled, but no overall hard cap is proven.

Text-only storage-backed expert streaming on the physical phone. Historical harness: 5 runs across contexts 512, 1024, and 2048, identical tokens, 28-38 MB arena, ~2.06-2.09 GiB peak RSS, 0.37-0.69 decode tokens/s. New bounded API smoke at context 512: JSON Hello! and SSE 4, normal stops with default thinking disabled, ~2.09 GiB peak RSS. API wall times are separate from historical decode throughput. No full-resident reference parity or hard process cap; long-form API qualification remains open.

32 layers, 32 experts, top-4, separate gate/up/down (down Q4_K in 16 layers and Q6_K in 16). Streamed token IDs and logits equal a resident run at the same prefill unit on the host and on the phone. On the phone resident decodes 8.29 tokens/s versus 4.44 streamed with the shipped cache and 1.92 with the layered preset, because the file fits in the page cache.
